body.p: Applicant initially expresses appreciation to the Examiner for the detailed Office Action provided. Applicant also expresses appreciation for the indication that the drawings are accepted, for the acknowledgment of the claim for foreign priority and receipt of the certified copy of the priority document, and for the acknowledgment and consideration of the Information Disclosure Statements filed on November 14, 2022 and December 6, 2023.
Upon entry of the present paper, claims 1-8 will have been amended. Thus, claims 1-9 will remain pending in the present application, with claims 1 and 8 being in independent form.

The herein-contained amendments are not an acquiescence in the propriety of the outstanding rejections. Instead, the claims are amended to even more clearly and explicitly set forth features of the present application, in accordance with the agreement reached during the telephone interview, as a sincere effort to advance prosecution. In this regard, it is submitted that the amendments contain no prohibited new matter. For example, the amendments are submitted to be supported at least by the following portions of the present application as filed: FIG. 6D; page 25, line 32 to page 26, line 19; and page 34, line 32 to page 35, line 5 ( [0108] and [0144] of corresponding U.S. Pat. Appl. Pub. No. 2023/0133086).

Applicant addresses the pending rejections below and respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal thereof together with an indication of allowability of claims 1-9 (i.e., all pending claims) in the next Official communication. Such action is respectfully requested and submitted to be appropriate for at least the reasons provided below.

Pages 2-4 of the Office Action identify a claim phrase/element (i.e., the obtainer in claim 1) which is being interpreted under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) as means-plus-function claim language. It is indicated that Applicant may amend the claims if Applicant does not intend for the identified phrase/element to be interpreted under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f).
By the present paper, without acquiescing in the propriety of the interpretation, the claims are amended to delete the identified phrase/element.

In view of the above, since the identified element/phrase no longer exists, it is submitted that the claims no longer invoke 35 U.S.C. § 112(f). Thus, it is requested that the claims be interpreted accordingly.

Claims 1-7 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention. Specifically, it is asserted that written description fails to disclose to disclose the corresponding structure, material, or acts for performing the function of the phrase/element of the claims which is being interpreted as means-plus-function claim language (i.e., the obtainer in claim 1).
By the present paper, without acquiescing in the propriety of the rejection and as discussed in the preceding section, the claims are amended to delete the identified phrase/element.

Accordingly, it is further submitted that the grounds of the above-captioned rejection are moot and no longer exist. As such, it is further requested that the above-captioned rejection be withdrawn in the next Official communication.

Claims 1, 5, and 7-9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Pat. Appl. Pub. No. 2018/0345790 to Mimura et al. (hereinafter "MIMURA") in view of Japanese Pat. Appl. Pub. No. 2018-073380 to Tamura (hereinafter "TAMURA").

As generally discussed above, without acquiescing in the propriety of the rejection, the claims are amended by the present paper in accordance with the results of the telephone interview. At least in view of the amendments, Applicant respectfully traverses the grounds of the above- captioned rejection as at least no longer existing.

For example, amended independent claim 1 is directed to a display control device that performs display control on a first display and a second display of a vehicle, with the second display being different from the first display.

According to the amended independent claim, the display control device obtains switching information indicating that switching between driving modes, including an autonomous driving mode and a manual driving mode, is to be performed in the vehicle. The display control device causes, before completion of a first switching, (i) the first display to display first information and third information and (ii) the second display to display second information when the switching information indicates that the first switching is to be performed.

In this regard: the first switching is from the autonomous driving mode to the manual driving mode; the first information indicates that the first switching is to be performed; the second information assists a user of the vehicle in driving in the manual driving mode; and the third information, which is displayed on the first display, indicates that the second display, which is different from the first display, is displaying the second information that assists the user of the vehicle in driving in the manual mode.

Thus, according to the features of amended independent claim 1, the third information, which is displayed on the first display, indicates that the second information, which is displayed on the second display (which is different from the first display), assists the user of the vehicle in driving in the manual mode.

Such features are supported and disclosed at least by FIG. 6D and page 25, line 32 to page 26, line 19 of the present application as filed ( [0108] of corresponding U.S. Pat. Appl. No. 2023/0133086). As shown and described by such non-limiting and exemplary embodiment, the (first) display 520 includes the image 624A, which includes the first information and the two arrows being an example of the third information. Such arrows, being an example of the third information displayed in the image 624A of the (first) display 520, indicate that the second display 500 (and also the second display 510) is displaying the second information 604A (and also the second information 614A) that assists the user of the vehicle in driving in the manual mode.

As generally discussed and agreed during the telephone interview, Applicant respectfully submits that MIMURA and TAMURA fail to disclose or render obvious such features of amended independent claim 1, at least relating to the third information, as recited by the claimed combination.

Instead, MIMURA discloses a vehicle system 1 that includes a human interface machine (HMI) 400, with the human interface machine 400 including a first display unit 450 and a second (heads-up) display unit 460. (See MIMURA at [0062] and [0111]). The first display unit 450 is configured to display information necessary for travel at a time of manual driving or at a time of automatic driving, such as a speed, an engine speed, a remaining fuel amount, a radiator water temperature, a travel distance, etc. (MIMURA at [0118]). The second (heads-up) display unit 460 is disposed at a position higher than the first display unit 450 (e.g., on a front windshield) and
displays a part of the information displayed on the first display unit 450. (MIMURA at [0119] and [0130]).

Specifically, MIMURA discloses that the first display unit 450 displays detailed information, while the second (heads-up) display unit 460 displays such information as simple information, of which an information amount is smaller than that of the detailed information. (MIMURA at [0131]. For example, the simple information may be information in which a type or a number of items displayed is smaller than the type or the number of items displayed as the detailed information (MIMURA at [0131]-[0132]).

MIMURA further discloses that an automatic driving control unit 300 performs a control for switching the vehicle from automatic driving to manual driving. (MIMURA at [0232]). In such case, an image for causing an occupant to execute the manual driving is displayed on one or both of the first display unit 450 and the second (heads-up) display unit 460. (MIMURA at FIG. 31 and [0232]). For example, FIG. 31 and FIG. 32 of MIMURA show a (first) third screen IM3- 10 and a (second) third screen IM3-10 (which is intensified) which are displayed on the first display unit 450 for requesting the occupant to perform a specific operation, and also show a (first) fourth screen IM4-10 and a (second) fourth screen IM4-10 which are displayed on the second (heads-up) display unit 460 as an animation for indicating the specific operation which is requested to be performed. (MIMURA at [0232]-[0237]).

Accordingly, as shown in FIG. 31 and FIG. 32, MIMURA displays the first (detailed) information on the first display unit 450, and displays the second (simple) information on the second (heads-up) display unit 460. Nevertheless, MIMURA does not disclose any third information, which is displayed on the first display unit 450, and which indicates that information
is displayed on the second (heads-up) display unit 460 that assists the occupant in driving in the manual mode. For example, FIG. 31 of MIMURA is reproduced below for convenience.

With respect to TAMURA, Applicant respectfully submits that this document fails to cure the above-discussed deficiencies of MIMURA. That is, TAMURA discloses that vehicle state notification information for notifying that the vehicle is in a predetermined state and an auxiliary notification part for supplementarily notifying a user that the vehicle state notification information is displayed on the information display body 204 are displayed. (See TAMURA at [0006]). For example, as shown in FIG. 8 of TAMURA, which is reproduced on the following page for convenience, release state information 590 indicating that the autonomous driving control is released is displayed and an emphasis display 591 (second information) for complementing the
release state information 590 is blinkingly displayed on an outline portion of the information display body 204. (See TAMURA at FIG.8 and [0051]-[0055]).

At least in view of the above and as generally discussed and agreed during the Telephone Interview, any propoer combination of MIMURA and TAMURA fails to arrive at the combination of features as now recited by amended indpendent claim 1. Thus, it is submitted that the grounds of the obviousness rejection of this claim at least no longer exist, and As such, it is requested that the rejection of claim 1 be withdrawn in the next Official communication.

Moreover, since independent claim 8 is amended by the present paper to recite similar features as discussed above with respect to amended independent claim 1, it is similarly submitted that the grounds of the rejection of this claim also at least no longer exist. As such, it is also requested that the rejection of claim 8 be withdrawn in the next Official communication

Further, since each of claims 5, 7, and 9 is directly dependent from one of amended independent claims 1 and 8, it is similarly submitted that these claims are not rendered obvious by MIMURA and TAMURA at least in view of their dependencies, and also in view of their further combinations of recited features. As such, it is also requested that the rejection of claims 5, 7, and
9 be withdrawn in the next Official communication. Rejection of Claims 2-4 and 6 under 35 U.S.C. & 103

Claim 2 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over MIMURA in view of TAMURA, and further in view of U.S. Pat. Appl. Pub. No. 2016/0098017 to Park et al. (hereinafter "PARK"). Claim 3 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over MIMURA in view of TAMURA, and further in view of U.S. Pat. Appl. Pub. No. 2019/0094856 to Kawate (hereinafter "KAWATE"). Lastly, claims 4 and 6 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over MIMURA in view of TAMURA, and further in view of U.S. Pat. Appl. Pub. No. 2016/0196247 to Lee et al. (hereinafter "LEE").
Applicant also respectfully traverses these grounds of rejection as at least no longer existing, at least for the reasons discussed above with respect to independent claim 1.

That is, claims 2-4 and 6 are each directly dependent from amended independent claim 1, which is again patentable over MIMURA and TAMURA for at least the reasons discussed supra. In this regard, Applicant respectfully submits that PARK, KAWATE, and LEE fail to cure the above-discussed deficiencies of MIMURA and TAMURA. Instead, PARK merely appears to be

relied upon to teach a notification icon which informs the user of an incoming call, KAWATE merely appears to be relied upon to teach gaze information regarding a gaze of a user, and LEE merely appears to be relied upon to teach various display styles. Nevertheless, none of these documents appears to disclose or teach the above-discussed features regarding the third information of amended independent claim 1.

As a result, it is submitted that PARK, KAWATE, and LEE fail to cure the deficiencies of MIMURA and TAMURA. As such, the grounds for the above-captioned rejections are also submitted to at least no longer exist and are requested to be withdrawn.

At least in view of the above, it is respectfully submitted that each and every pending claim of the present application (i.e., claims 1-9) meets the requirements for patentability. Thus, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw the outstanding rejections and to indicate the allowance of each and every pending claim in the present application.

In view of the fact that none of the art of record, whether considered alone, or in any proper combination thereof, discloses or renders obvious the pending claims of the present application, and in further view of the above amendments and remarks, reconsideration of the Examiner's action and allowance of the present application are respectfully requested and submitted to be appropriate.

Applicant notes that this amendment is being made to advance prosecution of the application to allowance, and should not be considered as surrendering equivalents of the territory between the claims prior to the present amendment and the amended claims. Further, no acquiescence as to the propriety of the Examiner's rejection is made by the present amendment. All amendments to the claims which have been made in this amendment, and which have not been specifically noted to overcome a rejection based upon the prior art, should be considered to have been made for a purpose unrelated to patentability, and no estoppel should be deemed to attach thereto.

Should an extension of time be necessary to maintain the pendency of this application, including any extensions of time required to place the application in condition for allowance by an Examiner's Amendment, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fee to Deposit Account No. 19-0089.
